name: Primo Events Calendar
author: Republic Salad

sections.description:
Primo Events Calendar puts your events on your website in minutes. Add an event, drop the calendar on a page, and visitors can browse by month, filter by category and add events to their own calendar.

It is built for venues, restaurants, community groups, churches, schools and small businesses that want a clean, fast calendar without a monthly fee.

What you get

  • Month calendar and event cards. Visitors switch between a monthly calendar and image cards, and can filter by category.
  • Recurring events. Weekly, every-two-weeks and monthly schedules, plus extra one-off dates, all from one event.
  • Reusable venues. Save a venue once and pick it on any event; the address fills in automatically.
  • Polished event pages. Date, time, time zone, venue, address and an optional “Register / Event Website” button.
  • Add to calendar. Google Calendar links and iCal / Outlook (.ics) downloads for the date a visitor picked.
  • Match your site. Accent color, card columns for desktop, tablet and mobile, calendar colors and an event time zone.
  • Works with Elementor and the block editor. Use the Shortcode block or Elementor’s Shortcode widget.
  • Bring your events with you. Import from CSV, JSON, XML, iCalendar (.ics), or a WordPress export from The Events Calendar or Eventline.
  • Getting-started checklist. New sites get a short checklist, including a one-click “Create calendar page” button.

Everything in this plugin is free: no license key, no trial, no locked features and no tracking.

Need ticket sales?

Primo Events Calendar Pro is an optional add-on from Republic Salad. It installs alongside this plugin and adds ticketing, Stripe checkout, QR-code check-in, attendee management, reporting and guest emails. This free plugin keeps working on its own, with or without Pro.

Shortcodes

  • [primevca_events] shows event cards with view controls.
  • [primevca_events view="month"] shows the monthly calendar.
  • [primevca_events view="list" limit="6"] shows six upcoming events.
  • Optional attributes: category="your-category-slug", month="YYYY-MM" and controls="no".

Copyable examples are under Events > Appearance.

Privacy and External Services

The calendar edition does not collect visitor registration details, run analytics tracking, send telemetry, or make background requests to external services. Event and venue information is stored in the site’s WordPress database and may be published publicly by the site owner. Avoid publishing private information in event descriptions or locations.

Google Calendar is optional. Only when a visitor clicks its link does their browser open Google with the selected event’s title, date/time, description, location, and event URL. Review Google’s terms and privacy policy before using that service:

  • Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

An external event link opens the destination chosen by the event author. iCalendar downloads are generated locally. Import files are parsed on the site’s server and are not sent to an external importer.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “Primo Events Calendar”, then Install and Activate.
  2. Follow the “Get started” checklist on your Dashboard: add your first event, then click “Create calendar page” to make a draft Events page with the monthly calendar.
  3. Review and publish the page.
  4. Optional: choose colors, card columns and a time zone under Events > Appearance.

You can also add [primevca_events] to any page yourself.
sections.faq:
Is it really free?

Yes. All calendar features work without a license, account or payment, and nothing expires.

Does it sell tickets or take payments?

Not on its own. This plugin publishes events. For ticket sales, Stripe payments and QR check-in, see the optional Primo Events Calendar Pro add-on.

Does it work with my theme and Elementor?

Yes. The calendar is added with a shortcode, which works in the block editor, classic editor and Elementor. Event pages can use your theme’s layout or the plugin’s own event page design (Events > Appearance).

Can I have repeating events?

Yes. Choose weekly, every two weeks or monthly, set an end date, and add extra dates if you need them. Each repeat appears in the calendar and cards. Extra dates use the original event’s time and length; create a separate event when those differ.

Which time zone is used?

The site time zone from Settings > General, unless you set an event time zone (for example America/Denver) under Events > Appearance.

Can I import events from another plugin?

Yes. Events > Import Events accepts CSV, JSON, XML, iCalendar files and WordPress export (WXR) files from The Events Calendar or Eventline.

Are private or password-protected events shown?

No. Private, draft and password-protected events are left out of public calendars and exports. A password-protected event page shows the WordPress password form first.

Does it work on multisite?

Activate it on each site separately. Network-wide activation is not supported.

What happens if I deactivate or delete it?

Your events, venues, categories and settings stay in the database. The plugin never deletes your content.

I’m upgrading from Eventline or the older Primo/Omirp plugin. What should I know?

Back up first. Deactivate the old plugin before activating this one and don’t run both. Then run the calendar data upgrade under Events > Appearance until it finishes. It converts your events, venues, categories and saved shortcodes ([primo_events], [omirp_events], [veridea_events]) without changing post IDs or event URLs, and keeps backups of the original data. Shortcodes written directly into theme files need updating by hand. Registration, payment and email records from the old full-feature plugin are not migrated by this free plugin.
sections.changelog:
2.3.5

  • Add a getting-started checklist on the Dashboard, Plugins screen and Events screens for new sites, with a one-click “Create calendar page” button. It disappears once an event and a calendar page exist, and can be dismissed.
  • Show event dates and times in the site’s date and time formats on event pages that use the theme’s layout (they previously showed raw values such as 2026-12-12T19:00), including the selected date of a repeating event and its time zone.
  • Rename the Events > “Pro — Coming Soon” page to “Pro Add-on” now that Pro is available.
  • Rewrite the plugin description and add screenshots.

2.3.4

  • Add an Events > Pro — Coming Soon information page describing the upcoming Pro add-on. It is hidden once Pro is active and never limits free features.
  • Add developer hooks for add-ons: primevca_single_event_after_details (single event pages), primevca_appearance_after_upgrade (Appearance screen), primevca_import_form_options and primevca_import_row_errors (importer).
  • Run alongside Primo Events Calendar Pro 3.0 and later, which is now an add-on; continue to stand down only for older standalone Pro 2.x releases.
  • Keep occurrence links created before the identifier change (omirp_date) selecting the right date.

2.3.3

  • Fix the category example in the Appearance shortcode reference (live-music).
  • Stand down with an admin notice when Primo Events Calendar Pro is active, instead of loading a second copy of the calendar. The calendar class now lives in includes/class-events-calendar.php and loads only after that check, so the two editions never declare the same class.
  • Refuse activation while Pro is active, with an explanatory message.

2.3.2

  • Address WordPress.org review findings: bind calendar download nonces to the event and occurrence and independently enforce publication and password access.
  • Respect password protection in the native event template, structured data, Google Calendar links and public calendar queries.
  • Separate save-handler post-type, autosave, revision, permission, nonce-shape and nonce-verification guards; bind edit nonces to the object ID.
  • Use distinctive primevca identifiers for post types, taxonomy, classes, settings, actions, metadata, shortcode and assets.
  • Add an administrator-only, nonce-protected, resumable upgrade for legacy calendar data and saved shortcodes.

2.3.1

  • Add a shortcode reference to Events > Appearance, with copyable examples for cards, monthly calendars, categories, a specific month, and combined options.
  • Explain shortcode attributes, category-filter settings, legacy aliases, and insertion in WordPress or Elementor.

2.3.0

  • Prepare the first calendar-only directory edition under the Primo Events Calendar name, by Republic Salad.
  • Align the installation folder, main plugin file, text domain, asset handles, and primary shortcode with primo-events-calendar.
  • Remove paid ticketing, purchaser communications, reporting, QR assets, and their runtime dependencies from this edition.
  • Retain legacy calendar data keys and shortcode aliases for existing event content.
  • Correct selected-occurrence handling in event pages.
  • Prevent simultaneous calendar initialization alongside the legacy full-feature plugin.
